chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you depart from Makkah to Al-Madina and reach Dhu al-Hulayfah, while you are returning to Al-Madina from Makkah, then go to the Mu'arras (resting place) of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If you are within the time for a prescribed prayer or an optional one, pray therein; and if it is outside the time for a prescribed prayer, then stay there for a while, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to rest there and pray.

key_terms.ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhu al-Hulayfah, the miqat (boundary) for pilgrims entering from Al-Madina
key_terms.مُعَرَّسَ النَّبِيِّ: The Prophet's resting place or encampment
key_terms.يُعَرِّسُ: To rest or encamp for a short period

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for visiting the Prophet's resting place when returning from Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the spiritual significance of Dhu al-Hulayfah, the Miqat for Medina, as a site of emulation (*ittiba'*) for the Prophet Muhammad (saww). It prescribes a specific ritual of rest and prayer at the Prophet's former encampment, reinforcing the concept of physical spaces holding enduring religious merit (*barakah*) in Shia jurisprudence. The instruction to pray even outside of obligatory times highlights the emphasis on voluntary devotion (*nawafil*) in conjunction with the Prophet's Sunnah.
